So, if someone enters the library with the intention to threaten the librarians, that seems like it would disrupt the calm environment. I wonder why someone would want to threaten librarians in the first place. Maybe they're upset about something, like a policy or a rule that the library has. But even if they're upset, threatening people doesn't seem like a good way to resolve the issue. It could make the situation worse and lead to more problems. Also, threatening someone is generally considered a form of intimidation, which is not okay. It can make people feel unsafe and uncomfortable, especially in a place that's supposed to be safe and welcoming. Librarians are there to help people, so threatening them goes against the purpose of the library. Maybe there are better ways to address any issues someone has with the library. I also think about the consequences of threatening someone. It could lead to legal actions, like being charged with harassment or assault. That's not something anyone wants to deal with. Plus, it would damage the person's reputation and relationships, which isn't worth it for whatever reason they had to threaten the librarians. In summary, entering a library to threaten the librarians seems wrong because it disrupts the peaceful environment, intimidates people who are there to help, and can lead to negative consequences. There are better ways to address any issues without resorting to threats.
